error_types.title: Variable not defined
error_types.explanation_with_var: '%1' doesn't exist at this point — it was never created, or was created in a different scope (e.g. inside a function).
error_types.fix_with_var: Check that '%1' is spelled correctly and created before this line.
error_types.explanation_generic: A variable name was used before it was created, or was misspelled.
error_types.fix_generic: Check spelling and that the variable is created before use.

error_types.title: Array index out of bounds
error_types.explanation_generic: You accessed a position in a list/array that doesn't exist. Lists start at index 0, so a list of 5 items has indices 0-4.
error_types.fix_generic: Check the array length before accessing. Use len(arr) and make sure your index < len(arr).

error_types.title: Wrong type

patterns.explanation_template: Cannot use '%1' between a %2 and a %3.
patterns.fix: Convert one side to the right type, e.g. int(x) or str(x).
Check the types of all values on this line using type(x).

error_types.explanation_generic: A value of the wrong type was passed or used. E.g. a number was expected but a string was given.
error_types.fix_generic: Check the types of all values on this line using type(x).

error_types.title: Division by zero
error_types.explanation_generic: The program divided a number by zero, which is mathematically undefined.
error_types.fix_generic: Add a check before dividing: if denominator != 0: ... else: handle_zero()

error_types.title: Attribute does not exist

patterns.explanation_template: The variable is None (empty/null), so calling .%1 on it fails. The function that was supposed to return an object returned None instead.
patterns.fix: Check that the object was actually created and is not None before calling methods on it.

patterns.explanation_template: A '%1' object doesn't have an attribute called '%2'. Check the object type and its available attributes.
patterns.fix: Use dir(obj) to see what attributes are available.

error_types.explanation_generic: Called a method or accessed a field that doesn't exist on this object.
error_types.fix_generic: Use dir(obj) to see what attributes are available.

error_types.title: File not found

patterns.explanation_template: The file '%1' doesn't exist at that path. The path may be wrong, or the file hasn't been created yet.
patterns.fix: Check the file path is correct. Use an absolute path or verify the working directory.

error_types.explanation_generic: A file path was provided that doesn't exist on disk.
error_types.fix_generic: Check the file path is correct. Use an absolute path or verify the working directory.

error_types.title: Memory access violation (segfault)
error_types.explanation_generic: The program tried to access memory it doesn't own. Common causes: buffer overflow, writing past the end of an array, or following a null/dangling pointer.
error_types.fix_generic: Check all array accesses are within bounds. Verify pointers are not NULL before dereferencing.

error_types.title: Invalid value

patterns.explanation_template: '%2' cannot be converted to %1. The string contains characters that are not a valid number.
patterns.fix: Validate the input before converting, e.g. if x.isdigit(): int(x)

error_types.explanation_generic: A value was passed that is the right type but outside the acceptable range or format.
error_types.fix_generic: Check what values are valid for this function and validate input before passing it.

error_types.title: Dictionary key not found

patterns.explanation_template: The key '%1' doesn't exist in the dictionary at this point.
patterns.fix_template: Use dict.get('%1', default) instead of dict['%1'] to avoid the crash.

error_types.explanation_generic: Tried to access a dictionary key that doesn't exist.
error_types.fix_generic: Use 'key in dict' to check before accessing, or use dict.get(key, default).

error_types.title: Infinite recursion
error_types.explanation_generic: A function kept calling itself without stopping. The call stack grew until Python ran out of room.
error_types.fix_generic: Make sure your recursive function has a base case that stops recursion. Check that the base case is reachable.

error_types.title: Module not found

patterns.explanation_template: Python can't find the module '%1'. It may not be installed, or the name might be misspelled.

error_types.explanation_generic: A required module or package is missing.
error_types.fix_generic: Check the module name and install it if needed with pip install <name>.

error_types.title: Indentation error
error_types.explanation_generic: Python is very strict about indentation (spaces/tabs at the start of lines). A line is not indented consistently with the block it belongs to.
error_types.fix_generic: Use 4 spaces per indent level consistently. Don't mix tabs and spaces.

error_types.title: Syntax error
error_types.explanation_generic: Python couldn't parse the code — something is written incorrectly. Common causes: missing colon after if/for/def, mismatched parentheses, or a typo in a keyword.
error_types.fix_generic: Check the line and the line before it for missing colons, brackets, or quotes.
